'''Sekba''' or sometimes called '''bektim''' is a [[Chinese Indonesian cuisine|Chinese Indonesian]] [[pork]] [[offal]]<ref name="Whitmarsh Wood 2013 p. 119">{{cite book | last1=Whitmarsh | first1=A. | last2=Wood | first2=M. | title=Jakarta: 25 Excursions in and Around the Indonesian Capital | publisher=Tuttle Publishing | year=2013 | isbn=978-1-4629-0893-6 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nhTRAgAAQBAJ&pg=PT119 | access-date=October 1, 2016 | page=119}}</ref> [[stew]]ed in a mild [[soy sauce]]-based soup. The stew tastes mildly sweet and salty, made from soy sauce, [[garlic]], and Chinese herbs. It is a popular fare [[street food]] in Indonesian Chinatowns, such as Gloria alley, [[Glodok]] Chinatown in [[Jakarta]], [[Indonesia]].<ref>{{cite news | title = Glodok's top five foods | work = Yahoo News | date = 26 March 2013 | url = https://sg.news.yahoo.com/glodok-top-five-foods-170000208.html}}</ref>
